market.domesticSlice: India-specific figures; the global parent's own market context is separate and not sized here

structureFacts: India's abrasives market is large and growing at a steady ~6% CAGR, but it is highly concentrated: Grindwell Norton (Saint-Gobain's Indian arm) and Carborundum Universal (CUMI) together control more than half of it (~26% and ~25-30% respectively) — a genuinely different structure from a fragmented category where a smaller player can win on niche positioning alone.

Global brand heritage does not automatically translate into Indian market share — a foreign parent's century-plus history and worldwide scale is a real asset, but the Indian market is dominated by two domestic-listed incumbents with direct Saint-Gobain/global-group backing of their own.

adoptionStructure.note: A B2B industrial-supply market (metalworking, construction, fabrication end-users) sold through distributors and direct industrial accounts — not a consumer or subscription market.

drivers: Product consistency/quality for industrial end-users (metalworking, construction, fabrication) where abrasive failure has real cost/safety consequences.
Distributor relationships and on-the-ground availability — an industrial buyer needs reliable local supply, not just a strong global brand name.
Certification/safety-standard compliance (e.g. oSa) as a baseline trust signal, particularly for larger industrial accounts with their own procurement compliance requirements.
customerValue.strongestPredictor: Local distribution reliability and account relationships — in a concentrated B2B market, a smaller player's growth depends more on winning and keeping specific industrial accounts than on brand awareness alone.
